name: Polyseat 0.3.2
body:
**One bug, on hosts where uhid is a module rather than built in, which is most
of them.** Like the one before it, it happens at boot and looks like anything
but what it is.

Seats are untouched by this release. Nothing in it changes how a seat is built,
so updating is a rebuild and a restart of the daemon and no more.

## The uhid observer restarted every thirty seconds, forever

The observer attaches a kprobe to `uhid_dev_create2` so that a gamepad can be
attributed to the container that created it as a fact rather than a guess. A
kprobe attaches to a symbol the running kernel has, and where uhid is a module
its symbols do not exist until it is loaded.

Nothing loads it in time. `/dev/uhid` is a static node, declared in
`modules.devname` and created at boot by systemd-tmpfiles, and the module is
autoloaded only when something first opens that node, which is the first seat
that runs a pad. So the daemon starts seconds into boot, finds no symbol, and
retries until somebody happens to plug in a controller.

**It hides well.** The node exists either way, so every check passed and
everything looked correctly installed. The one place that would have said
otherwise, the warning in the interface that reads "load the uhid module", tests
for the node and could therefore never fire on the machine it was written for.

Found on CachyOS 7.2.0, where `CONFIG_UHID=m`. It was never seen on the
development machine because bluez had already loaded uhid there for HID over
GATT.

**Nothing was broken while it was happening.** Gamepads worked. The broker fell
back to attributing them by name, which is the documented fallback, and a
heuristic rather than a fact.

`host/prepare.sh` now loads uhid and writes `/etc/modules-load.d/polyseat.conf`
so it is loaded at the next boot too, which is the boot that matters.

## A supervised helper can now be given up on

`supervise.Failed` had been declared and documented since the daemon was written
and was set nowhere, so the supervisor could not stop trying.

A helper may now name the exits that will still be true in thirty seconds, and
the observer names the one that means this kernel has no symbol to watch. It
says so once, in the log and in the interface, and stops. Brokers are unchanged
and still retry everything, which is right for them: most ways a broker dies are
ways it might not die next time.

The interface tells "gave up" and "not running" apart, because they want
different sentences and the first one names a cause and a command.

## Updating

```
sudo host/update.sh
```

Or by hand:

```
git fetch --tags
git checkout v0.3.2
sudo host/install.sh
```

Either way the daemon is rebuilt and restarted and `prepare.sh` runs again,
which is what loads uhid and writes the modules-load entry. Existing seats are
not touched and do not need rebuilding.
